name: forces
title: Force diagram (free body)
tagline: Free-body force diagram: labelled arrows from a body, lengths derived from newtons; resultant and balanced/unbalanced verdict always derived and occludable.
description: A free-body force diagram — one object in a scene (a box on a surface, a hanging mass, a falling or floating body) with labelled force arrows drawn from its centre. The author writes only the scene and each force's name, magnitude in newtons and direction (a cardinal up/down/left/right or a bearing in degrees); every arrow's length is derived from its newtons against one shared scale, so a weak force can never be drawn long. The resultant force (its magnitude and direction) and the balanced-or-unbalanced verdict are always derived from the exact component sum of the forces — there is nowhere to author them. A force value can be occluded ("what is this force?"), and with balanceOne the hidden value is the derived complement that balances the rest (anti-leak). The resultant can be occluded ("find the resultant"), one arrow highlighted, and the whole thing built one force per stage. Covers balanced vs unbalanced forces, Newton's first law, finding a resultant (including the diagonal 3-4-5 case by Pythagoras) and the terminal-velocity story as a staged sequence.
whenToUse: Reach for this to draw a free-body / force diagram whenever forces act on an object: balanced vs unbalanced forces, Newton's first law (steady speed = balanced), finding a resultant force, and terminal velocity. Set the scene to the physical context (box-on-ground, hanging, falling, floating, free) — it draws the object glyph and any support furniture. Give each force its name (label), magnitude (newtons) and direction: dir for the usual axis-aligned case ("up"/"down"/"left"/"right" — weight down, normal contact up, thrust right, drag left), or bearing in degrees clockwise from up for a slanted force. Every arrow length is derived from the newtons on one shared scale, and the resultant + verdict are derived from the forces — you never author a length, a resultant or a verdict. Common configurations: BALANCED — equal opposite forces (weight 500 down, normal 500 up) → the verdict reads "balanced, 0 N"; UNBALANCED — thrust 800 right, drag 300 left → resultant 500 N right; FIND THE RESULTANT — occlude: "resultant" hides the derived magnitude/direction and verdict for a question; WHAT FORCE BALANCES THIS? — give the known forces, add the unknown force with only its direction + an id, and set balanceOne to that id so its newtons is derived as the complement that balances the rest (its value shows "?", anti-leak); THE DIAGONAL HARD CASE — a 3 N right and a 4 N down give a 5 N resultant by Pythagoras (keep authored forces perpendicular so it stays GCSE-safe). Staged builds read well: set reveal to add one force per stage (base = the object with the first force), bring the resultant in on the last stage; the terminal-velocity story is a sequence of blocks — weight only (accelerating), weight vs growing drag, then balanced at terminal velocity. Toggle show.resultant, show.verdict, show.values, show.grid. Keep the same scene and newton scale across a lesson so pupils compare like with like. Synonyms a teacher might use: free-body diagram, force diagram, resultant force, net force, balanced forces, unbalanced forces, Newton's first law, terminal velocity, weight, normal reaction, thrust, drag, air resistance, tension, friction.

scene.description: The physical context, which draws the object and any support furniture. "box-on-ground": a box resting on a ground line. "hanging": a mass on a string from a ceiling. "falling": a body in the air (skydiver / raindrop) with no support. "floating": a body in water with a waterline. "free": a plain body with no scene furniture (a puck, a general object). Default "free".

label.description: The force's name, drawn beside its arrow — "Weight", "Air resistance", "Thrust", "Normal contact force", "Tension". Omit for an unlabelled arrow.

newtons.description: The magnitude of the force in newtons (positive). The arrow's LENGTH is derived from this against the shared scale — you never set a length. Omit only when this force is the one balanceOne solves for (its value is then derived).

dir.description: The force's direction as a cardinal: up / down / left / right. Use this for the usual axis-aligned free-body diagram (weight down, normal up, thrust right, drag left). Give EITHER dir OR bearing, not both.

bearing.description: The force's direction as a bearing in degrees measured CLOCKWISE from straight up (0 = up, 90 = right, 180 = down, 270 = left). Use for a slanted force (a rope at an angle). Give EITHER dir OR bearing. Keep the hard case perpendicular so the resultant is a clean Pythagorean value — no trig beyond Pythagoras at GCSE.

occlude.description: Render this force's newton value as "?" — the "what is this force?" hook. The arrow still draws (at its true length). Default false.

highlight.description: Draw this arrow in amber to draw the eye to one force. Default false.

id.description: Optional kebab-case identifier, only needed so balanceOne can name which force it solves for (e.g. "friction").

forces.description: The forces acting on the object, each drawn as an arrow from the body centre. Write each force's name, newtons and direction — the length, the resultant and the verdict are all derived.

resultant.description: How to present the DERIVED resultant. The resultant itself (magnitude + direction) is always computed from the forces — this object only styles/occludes it.

occlude.description: Hide the resultant magnitude and direction (and the verdict) as "?" — the "find the resultant force" hook. The resultant arrow is not drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the resultant arrow and readout in amber emphasis. Default true when the resultant is shown (the resultant IS the result).

balanceOne.description: The id of ONE force whose magnitude is UNKNOWN and DERIVED as the complement that makes the whole system balance (resultant zero) — the "what force balances these?" hook. Give that force its direction + id and omit its newtons; its value renders as "?" (anti-leak) and the system is treated as balanced. If the named force's direction cannot balance the rest, its value is left unknown.

show.description: Furniture toggles (all default true unless stated).

resultant.description: Draw the resultant arrow (dashed, from the centre) and its readout. false shows the forces only. Default true (false when balanceOne is set — a balanced system has no resultant to draw).

verdict.description: Show the "Balanced" / "Unbalanced" readout beneath the figure. Default true.

values.description: Write each force's newton value beside its name. false shows names only (or names hidden too if unlabelled) — an answer space. Default true.

grid.description: Show a faint square background grid (helps read arrow lengths / components). Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

reveal.description: Staged build: draw only the first N forces (and the resultant only once all authored forces are shown). Omit to draw everything. The base of a staged build is reveal 1 (the object with its first force); bring the resultant in last.
